text: Alison, great to be here. We've introduced ourselves so everyone knows who we are. I think many people would be surprised that there's a trade association for not just crypto, not just a blockchain, but staking. Can you talk a little bit about the reason behind the proof of Stake Alliance?
speaker: A

text: Yeah, sure. So the proof of Stake alliance was founded in 2019. So I have been talking about staking policy for some six years now and the idea behind it. Originally this was around the time when some of the first proof of stake chains were launching and some of the first staking as a services businesses were starting to commercialize their offerings. And we quickly realized that in order for them to go to market effectively, we would need some sort of regulatory clarity and on both the security side and also on the tax side. So we came together as an industry at that time and said let's start putting together some legal white papers, let's go down to D.C. we'll meet with Congress, we'll meet with SEC and try to put together some rules of the road for staking and some industry best practices. So we published our first set of industry best practices in 2020. We updated those in 2023. And we're still working with industry to this day, bigger and better than ever to try to get some sensible regulation for folks involved in the staking industry and in proof of stake ecosystems like Solana.
speaker: B

text: Very interesting. So staking is obviously literally existential to a chain like Solana that's existed for many, many years. And I come from Marinade. We have something like 2 billion US or 10 million SOL locked up. So this is a mature thing. How soon are we going to get this figured out? Like, are we 1% of the way there from a regulatory standpoint? 99. And what's going to happen this year? It has to be guaranteed, whatever you.
speaker: A

text: So if I'm being honest, I would say we're probably about 25% of the way there's. And that's real progress based on where we were before, especially when you look at the agencies. When you look at the SEC in particular, we've had some really good faith interactions with the agency and they've been moving very quickly. We've seen more from them on staking and engaging with the industry in the past four months than we have in the past four years. When I talk about constructive engagement, because as everyone knows, under the previous administration it was enforcement action after enforcement action after enforcement action. And they were trying to draw a direct line from lending to staking on the one hand, but also made this assertion that all staking services are investment contracts, which we know is not right. These are technical services, not financial services. So I say 25% of the way there because we have made some real strides, but we still don't have staking guidance. And that's something we've been pushing on for a long time. You've seen the SEC recently issued guidance on proof of work mining. And we as an industry, some 30 industry players, plus all of the major trades, including the Solana Policy Institute, the Digital Chamber, CCI Blockchain association, all came together last month and said we need the same treatment for staking as we have for proof of work mining. And so I think there's constructive dialogue. And actually, earlier this week, Commissioner Purse said at SEC Speaks that she personally supports guidance on proof of stake. So we're seeing a lot of positive momentum, but until we get that clarity, we're not fully there. And by the way, that's just on the security side, not even talking about tax.

speaker: A

text: Yeah, you would think it'd be pretty straightforward. So there are many tax issues that we pay attention to, but one of the main issues that we've been paying attention to, the first time we met with treasury about this issue was in 2019, actually. And it's about the taxation of stake staking rewards and in particular the timing. Right. So the question is, should these staking rewards be taxed at the time of creation or at the time of sale? And we say at the time of sale, it should be treated like all other created property. If you bake a loaf of bread, you're not taxed when it comes out of the oven, you're taxed when you sell it. So it should be the same thing for these newly created tokens that are being generated by the network. We thought that was pretty straightforward. And we think that's the case, by the way, under existing law. For a long time, IRS did not issue any guidance on the matter. And there was 2014 guidance on Bitcoin mining, but nothing on staking. And then when they finally did issue a statement, they said that staking rewards should be treated as services income, which we disagree with. So we're trying to continue to engage with them. But we've also seen positive sides from Congress. There was a standalone bill that was actually introduced last year that would clarify that both mining and staking rewards should just be taxed at the time of sale. And we just think that's fair treatment. So actively working on that issue. We've also actively been working on issues pertaining to liquid staking. So we did write the first legal analysis of liquid staking under the securities and commodities laws. But we also wrote a paper, this was in 2023, about when you go in and out of a receipt token, is that a taxable event? And actually, it's not Right. So we just think people need that clarity. And we'll continue to work on the tax issues simultaneously while we work on some of these other issues.
